recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-7902 unless a future work group reopens the broader policy for moving concepts between extensions and core elements.
issue_request: FHIR-7902 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 change request asking why FHIR Core Profile extensions, such as the FHIR Core Goal Profile, were not core resource elements. The approved resolution was to update defining-extensions.html to explain the core-element threshold and the role of standard extensions.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit 670cce6d0442b1b898ca8f9c9160ec1d73fbe4ed, matching Jira's SVN #6777 comment. That commit added the Core Elements subsection to source/defining-extensions.html; commit 9cf34511a41da2cf55df5f4c9672471d8d05a504 immediately corrected wording while preserving the rule.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml lists Defining Extensions as a current build page, source/fhir.ini has active extension profile inputs, and current source/defining-extensions.html also keeps HL7 extension-publishing guidance that explains why HL7 publishes standard extensions outside the base resource structure. Searches found no later Jira, Zulip, or Confluence evidence reversing this decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current source already says core elements are based on significant worldwide usage, otherwise concepts remain extensions, and HL7 can publish or ballot those extensions for interoperable use.
